result.topic_en: Riemann's Latin draft for the Paris prize question on heat conduction: he states the general problem of which conductivity properties keep the members of a given family of curves isothermal, writes the anisotropic heat equation and its variational form, and transforms it to new variables using quadratic forms, adjoint forms and determinants.
result.transcription:
Quaestionem ab Ill^{ma} Academia propositam ita tractabimus, ut prius {+eam [?] quae [?]+} quaestionem generaliorem solvamus
Quales esse debeant proprietates corporis motum caloris determinantes & distributio caloris, ut [-lineae-] [-...-] {+detur systema linearum+} lineae, quae [-...-] semper isothermae maneant.
Deinde ex solutione generali hujus problematis eos casus seligamus, in quibus proprietates illae [-evadant-] {+evadant+} ubique eaedem sive corpus [-...-] {+est+} homogeneum.
[-Primum quaestionem et aggrediamur-], considerandus est motus caloris in corpore qualicunque, {+Quam+} [-tamen-] {+tamen+} disquisitionem ad eum casum restringimus, in quo [-radiatio inter bina puncta-] [-fluxus caloris-] {+conductibilitas [?] ea [?]+} {+binis [?]+} idem est in directionibus oppositis. [-Denique-]
Tum si $u$ designat temperaturam tempore $t$ in puncto $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$,

$\mathrm{I}\quad \frac{\partial\, a_{1,1}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_1} + a_{1,2}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_2} + a_{1,3}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_3}}{\partial x_1} + \qquad = h\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$

[-designantibus quantitatibus-]
designando per $a$ conductibilitates resultantes et per $h$, functiones datas ipsarum $x_1, x_2, x_3$.
$a_{\iota,\iota'} = a_{\iota',\iota}$
$h$ calor specificus pro unitate voluminis sive productum ex calore specifico in densitatem.

[-Haec aequat-]
$(A)\quad \delta \iiint \sum_{\iota,\iota'} a_{\iota,\iota'}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_{\iota'}}\, dx_1\, dx_2\, dx_3 + \iiint 2h\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\,\delta u\, dx_1\, dx_2\, dx_3$
per corpus extensum [-totum-] a valore {+variationis+} [-...-] $\delta u$ in superficie pendeat. Forma $\begin{pmatrix} a_{1,1} & a_{2,2} & a_{3,3} \\ a_{1,2} & & \end{pmatrix}$ est forma positiva.
{+Quum calor a+}
[-Iam est-] Quodsi loco [-variabilis-] coordinatarum rectangularium $x_1, x_2, x_3$ tres variabiles independentes novae $s_1, s_2, s_3$ introducantur,

$(B)\quad \delta \iiint \sum_{\iota,\iota'} b_{\iota,\iota'}\frac{\partial u}{\partial s_\iota}\frac{\partial u}{\partial s_{\iota'}}\, ds_1\, ds_2\, ds_3 + \iiint 2k\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\,\delta u\, ds_1\, ds_2\, ds_3$

[-Tum sint formae secundi gradus a-]
[-Sint-] $\begin{pmatrix} b_{1,1} & b_{2,2} & b_{3,3} \\ b_{2,3} & b_{1,2} & b_{3,1} \end{pmatrix}$ $\begin{pmatrix} \beta_{1,1} & \beta_{2,2} & \beta_{3,3} \\ \beta_{1,2} & \beta_{2,1} & \beta_{3,1} \end{pmatrix}$ determinantes $A$, $B$ et formae adjunctae
[-Formae adjunctae hae-].
$a_{1,1}\quad a_{2,2}\quad a_{3,3}$ $\begin{pmatrix} \alpha_{1,1} & \alpha_{2,2} & \alpha_{3,3} \end{pmatrix}$
$a_{1,2}\quad a_{1,2}$

[-Erit-] [-$d_{\iota,\iota'}$ $ds_\iota ds$-]
$\sum a_{\iota,\iota'}\frac{\partial s_\mu}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial s_\nu}{\partial x_{\iota'}}\, \frac{1}{\sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}} = b_{\mu,\nu}$ $\qquad \frac{h}{\sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}} = k$
[-Iam est determinans systematis-]
$\begin{matrix} a_{1,1} & a_{1,2} & a_{1,3} \\ a_{1,2} & & \\ a & & a_{3,3} \end{matrix}$
determinans $A$ et determinantes partiales $\alpha_{\iota,\iota'}$, et [-systematis quantitatum $b$-] {+determinans determinantes+} $B$ et $\beta_{\iota,\iota'}$
invenitur [-...-] $= B \sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}$
$\beta_{\mu,\nu} = \sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'}\frac{\partial x_\iota}{\partial s_\mu}\frac{\partial x_{\iota'}}{\partial s_\nu}$
unde
$\sum_{\iota,\iota'} \alpha_{\iota,\iota'}\, dx_\iota\, dx_{\iota'} = \sum_{\iota,\iota'} \beta_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, ds_{\iota'}$

methods.what: Heat conduction equation in an anisotropic inhomogeneous body with symmetric conductivity coefficients
methods.quote: $\mathrm{I}\quad \frac{\partial\, a_{1,1}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_1} + a_{1,2}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_2} + a_{1,3}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_3}}{\partial x_1} + \qquad = h\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$

methods.what: Variational formulation of the heat equation, with the conductivity quadratic form positive definite
methods.quote: $(A)\quad \delta \iiint \sum_{\iota,\iota'} a_{\iota,\iota'}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x_{\iota'}}\, dx_1\, dx_2\, dx_3 + \iiint 2h\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\,\delta u\, dx_1\, dx_2\, dx_3$

methods.what: The same variational form expressed in new curvilinear variables s
methods.quote: $(B)\quad \delta \iiint \sum_{\iota,\iota'} b_{\iota,\iota'}\frac{\partial u}{\partial s_\iota}\frac{\partial u}{\partial s_{\iota'}}\, ds_1\, ds_2\, ds_3 + \iiint 2k\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\,\delta u\, ds_1\, ds_2\, ds_3$

methods.what: Transformation rule for the conductivity coefficients under a change of variables (divided by the Jacobian)
methods.quote: $\sum a_{\iota,\iota'}\frac{\partial s_\mu}{\partial x_\iota}\frac{\partial s_\nu}{\partial x_{\iota'}}\, \frac{1}{\sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}} = b_{\mu,\nu}$

methods.what: Transformation rule for the specific heat (divided by the Jacobian)
methods.quote: $\frac{h}{\sum \pm \frac{\partial s_1}{\partial x_1}\frac{\partial s_2}{\partial x_2}\frac{\partial s_3}{\partial x_3}} = k$

methods.what: Transformation of the adjoint form (minors), giving invariance of the quadratic differential form
Invariance of the adjoint quadratic differential form

items.quote: Quaestionem ab Ill^{ma} Academia propositam ita tractabimus, ut prius {+eam [?] quae [?]+} quaestionem generaliorem solvamus
items.english: We shall treat the question proposed by the most illustrious Academy by first solving a more general question.

items.quote: Quales esse debeant proprietates corporis motum caloris determinantes & distributio caloris, ut [-lineae-] [-...-] {+detur systema linearum+} lineae, quae [-...-] semper isothermae maneant.
items.english: What the properties of the body determining the motion of heat, and the distribution of heat, must be so that there is a given system of lines which always remain isothermal.

items.quote: Deinde ex solutione generali hujus problematis eos casus seligamus, in quibus proprietates illae [-evadant-] {+evadant+} ubique eaedem sive corpus [-...-] {+est+} homogeneum.
items.english: Then from the general solution of this problem we shall select those cases in which those properties turn out the same everywhere, i.e. the body is homogeneous.

items.quote: Quam+} [-tamen-] {+tamen+} disquisitionem ad eum casum restringimus, in quo [-radiatio inter bina puncta-] [-fluxus caloris-] {+conductibilitas [?] ea [?]+} {+binis [?]+} idem est in directionibus oppositis.
items.english: We restrict this investigation, however, to the case in which the conductivity is the same in opposite directions.
